input.title: janitor sweep test: the stateless-item fixture still labels its item with the retired origin marker
input.body:
`packs/basics/task-janitor-queue-sweep.test.mjs` has one fixture for the stateless-item repair — an open work item wearing no state label at all — and it builds that item with `['origin:schedule']`.

That marker is retired (#1064, DESIGN §15.26): nothing writes it and nothing branches on it. The fixture still passes, because what it needs is "some label that is not a state label" and the retired one qualifies — but it reads as though the marker means something to the sweep, which it does not, and the next reader has to check.

**The ask:** give that fixture a label that is plainly incidental (or none at all, if the sweep's contract is "no state label and no `needs-human`"), so the test says what it is testing. One test file; no production code should change. The existing assertion — the item comes back in `out.stateless` and is parked — must still hold.

This is also the first live exercise of the request mode landed in #1067: it is a real, small ask, deliberately chosen so the run has something honest to do.

Refs #1010

Comment class: other

Phase 1 merged as [#1067](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1067). **Phase 2's first trace is complete, on this repo**, and it answers the one thing Phase 1 could not verify.

## The happy path, end to end (2026-08-19 23:00–23:06 UTC)

[#1074](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1074) marked `claude-task` + `claude-model:sonnet` → tick → [#1075](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1075) → session → [#1076](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1076), six minutes end to end. Every step of §16 behaved as designed:

- **Labels ensured** by the tick before anything was marked — `claude-task` exists in the picker with its colour and description.
- **Adoption**: item titled `[claudinite-work] engine/implement-request #1074`, body `Request: #1074` / `Model: sonnet`, born `task:ready`. Both marks consumed, `claude-queued` on, one comment naming the item and the family.
- **Pickup**: precondition passed, claim + hand-off + one session, item to `task:agent`.
- **The run**: the ask was a one-line test-fixture change; the PR is exactly that, no production code, ceiling respected (opened, not merged).
- **Converge**: item parked open at `needs-human` + `task:needs-human-approval`; #1074 swapped `claude-queued` → `claude-in-review` with the PR and the model named.

**The permission API answers under the executor workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN`.** That was the open risk — the sandbox proxy-blocks `api.github.com`, so it could not be settled at landing. A failed read would have parked #1075 at `task:needs-human-failure` with the status on it; instead the verdict passed on the read. No workflow permission needed adding.

## What Phase 2 found

The item's Context rendered as two near-identical bullets — adoption writes one, the precondition added another — in the one section the session is told to read as its binding scope. [#1077](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1077) drops the precondition's.

## Still not verified, and why

The **unauthorized-mark refusal** (the plan's second Phase 2 trace). It needs an issue whose author has no push access here; every identity available to this session is the owner's, so it cannot be staged, and the adoption→pickup window the withdrawal variant would need is seconds wide (the drain follows the tick in the same run). The engine tests cover both shapes against the real executor with a fake GitHub — S45's disarm and S48's withdrawal — but the live trace is a human's to produce, from a second account, and it is the one thing left on this issue.
